cards.claim: Weight initialization accounting for dropout variance improves convergence and final accuracy on CIFAR-10
cards.conditions: VGG-like convolutional network on CIFAR-10, trained for 150 epochs with Nesterov momentum and tuned learning rates; network uses dropout with 70%, 60%, 60%, 50% keep rates at different layers; L2 regularization strength 5×10⁻⁴
cards.effect: 7.41% test error with dropout-corrected initialization vs 24.65% with He initialization (Nesterov momentum); 9.51% vs 10.54% with Adam optimizer. Paper notes the He initialization 'rendered the network untrainable for more learning rates' at certain settings.
cards.evidence: Experimental comparison on CIFAR-10 with two optimizers, convergence curves shown in Figure 4
cards.quote: We want that [variance of input] and [variance of gradient]. [...] Therefore, if [W] has its columns sampled uniformly from the surface of a unit hypersphere or is an orthonormal matrix, then our initialization is [formula accounting for dropout keep rate k and nonlinearity factor c_f]. [...] Ultimately, our initialization provided more consistent, quick, and accurate convergence.

cards.claim: Reestimating Batch Normalization variance parameters after training (with dropout off) improves test accuracy on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100
cards.conditions: DenseNet architectures on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 without data augmentation, trained with dropout and Batch Normalization; variance reestimation done by feeding training data forward one epoch with dropout disabled
cards.effect: CIFAR-10: 5.62% → 5.38% error (improvement of 0.24 percentage points); CIFAR-100: improvements of up to 2% (e.g., 23.91% → 22.48%, or 22.65% → 22.17%). Paper states 'can sometimes improve accuracy by more than 2%'.
cards.evidence: Table 2 showing DenseNet results with and without BN variance reestimation ('BN Update' columns); compared against prior state-of-the-art numbers from original DenseNet paper
cards.quote: Batch Normalization's variance estimates are greater when dropout is active because a neuron's input variance is greater with dropout. But dropout is deactivated during testing, and the variance estimates Batch Normalization normally uses are accurate when dropout is active not inactive. For this reason, we re-estimate the Batch Normalization variance parameters after training. We accomplish this by simply feeding forward the training data with dropout deactivated and only letting the Batch Normalization variance running averages update.
